result: The candidate is usable: the pinned code supports a four-trap stacked design with seven independent fix groups. The record is in `/Users/dev/terminal-bench/cwe-bench/stacking/out/reader/h3-ghsa-4mx9-3c2h-hwhg.json`. I wrote the JSON by hand and didn't run a validator on it. **The pinned commit comes before both fixes.** There is no `SanitizeSVG` anywhere in `kernel/`, and the newest changelog is v3.5.9. Both advisories (A, CVE-2026-29183, and B, the `data:text/xml` bypass) are therefore open at the pin. I couldn't read either fix commit from this tree. So whether A's code leaves B open, and whether B sits in code A wrote, are recorded as `null`, and the masking note relies on the advisory summary. **Current protection:** the only guard is `util.RemoveScriptsInSVG` (`kernel/util/misc.go:235`). It removes only elements named exactly `script` and is skipped when the `AllowSVGScript` setting is on. In the icon endpoint, the type 8 `content` text goes into the SVG unescaped (`kernel/api/icon.go:584`), and that endpoint needs no login (`kernel/api/router.go:36`). **Traps recorded (T1–T10), seven independent groups:** - **Advisory route:** T1 and T2, the unescaped icon content and the `data:text/xml` shape. One fix closes both. - **Same weak helper on the assets route:** T3, plus T8, the HTML importer that writes SVG files into assets. - **Raw SVG with no guard at all:** - T4: the history and repo-diff routes, which are admin-only. - T5: the emoji route. - T6: the public folder, which is unauthenticated on purpose. - **Others:** - T7: a namespaced `svg:script` element could pass the helper's exact-name check. - T9: an ordering trap. Stored block titles are expanded into the icon content after the raw input is read. - T10: a must-keep-working case. Template and plain-text icons have to keep rendering. **Proposed design: T2, T4, T5, T7, with T10 as a hidden must-keep test.** - T2 is the advisory anchor. - T4 and T5 are the DeepSeek-type traps. Each has a different reason to dismiss it: "admin-only" for T4, "emojis load via ``, where scripts don't run" for T5. - T7 is the MiMo-type trap. It stays open even if a solver adds attribute and link filtering. - I left out T6 because sanitising the public folder would break a published feature. I left out T9 because it is only independent if the solver validates the input instead of escaping the output. **Fairness risks:** these must keep working: - the `AllowSVGScript=true` setting; - logged-out access to the icon endpoint; - template icons; - legitimate `data:image/png` and `https` links. Widgets and plugins serve active content by design and are not traps. **Not verified** (listed under `unverified`): - T7's parser and browser behaviour was reasoned from the code, not run. - Who can write files into the emoji folder (T5) wasn't traced. - Whether stored block titles can carry markup through to the icon (T9) wasn't tested. Effort estimate: about 75 minutes.
